title: allium vineale subsp. affine
intro: Allium vineale subsp. affine, commonly known as wild garlic, is a subspecies of the wild garlic plant that belongs to the Allium genus. It has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, which include reducing inflammation and acting as an antibacterial agent, which can help alleviate respiratory issues, such as colds and congestion. The therapeutic actions of Allium vineale subsp. affine include expectorant, antiseptic, and anti-inflammatory properties, which can aid in relieving coughs, sore throats, and bronchitis. The bioactive constituents of the plant include flavonoids, glycosides, and organosulfur compounds, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
